# Climb batch 35, rung A: an exit out of an atomic block keeps the block's writes, on both paths (row 1039)

- problem: an exit out of an `atomic` block to an enclosing `label` lost the block's writes on both paths, as the batch's probes measured on the base: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-35/probes/fixes-35.md:19` (walk) and `:43` (compiled); ledger row 1039.
- spec: `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:59-63`, section "Atomic Expressions": "If it completes abruptly by exiting to an enclosing \KWD{label} expression, writes within the block are retained and become visible to other threads."
- precedent: the commit at a normal end of the same block, on each path: `BaseTask.endTransaction` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:210-221`) and the commit in `FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/tasks/FortressTaskRunner.java:125-131`); and the shape of `leaveTransaction`'s own branch for `TXLeave`, whose stale abort takes the abort path (`BaseTask.java:310-316`).
- deviation: none from the specification. From the precedent: the compiled exit's commit runs in the block's handler, after the task's transaction is set back to the parent (`BaseTask.java:302`), where `endTransaction` sets it after the commit; the commit uses only the transaction object, so the order changes nothing it does.
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java` and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/tasks/FortressTaskRunner.java`, both files of the original 2012 tree (`BaseTask.leaveTransaction` itself is the revival's, `594da41299`; `doItOnce` is the team's).

One launch of the worker role worked this rung: the worktree did not exist when it started.

## What changed and why

Commits on `wip/rung-exit-out-of-atomic`: `eb2f652487` (the tests and the fix), `8bd7cfcf0a` (the expected failure of a sibling defect, NEW-A-1), and the commit that adds this report and `record.md`.

- Compiled (`BaseTask.leaveTransaction`, `BaseTask.java:284-323`). Every compiled `atomic` block's handler takes every throwable of its body or its commit and calls `leaveTransaction` (`CodeGen.forAtomicBlock`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:2067-2100`, unchanged). An exit is a thrown `LabelExit` (F-373). `leaveTransaction` now commits the block's transaction when what leaves is a `LabelExit` (`BaseTask.java:303-309`): `transaction.TXCommit()` and `ftr.recordEndTransaction()`, the two calls of `endTransaction`. A commit that fails throws `TransactionAbortException`, which the branch takes as `t`, and the existing abort code then runs the block again where the abort names this transaction, or throws it on to the block of the ancestor that it names (`BaseTask.java:317-322`), as at a normal end, where the commit's abort reaches the same handler. Any other exception still goes through `TXLeave` and discards the writes (`:310-316`). The exit is thrown on after a commit that succeeds, so the label's handler takes it as before. A nested block's commit hands its reads and writes to its parent (`Transaction.TXCommit`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:302-307`), so an exit that leaves a nested block and its outer one commits the inner into the outer, then the outer.
- Walk (`FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce`, `FortressTaskRunner.java:122-148`). Walk runs an atomic block in `doItOnce`, which committed only after a normal end and gave the transaction up uncommitted in its `finally`, so the cells kept the block's writes under a transaction that stayed active and was then aborted by the next reader (`interpreter/env/ReferenceCell.java`, `getValue`). A `catch (LabelException exit)` now commits as the normal end does and throws the exit on (`:133-141`); a commit that fails aborts the transaction and throws `AbortedException`, so that `doIt` runs the block again, as at a normal end. `NamedLabelException`, walk's exit with a target, extends `LabelException`. `forAtomicExpr` and `forTryAtomicExpr` both run `doItOnce` (`interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:189`, `:216`).

The code generator is unchanged, so no compiled jar changes; the edit is in the runtime, which every compiled program loads.

## The tests: failing on the base, passing after

The two expected failures were promoted before the edit: `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss` became `tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`, and `compiler_tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.{fss,test}` became `compiler_tests/ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.{fss,test}` (`tests=ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`, `link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`); `ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test` takes the new name. Each test holds three cases: the single exit (`g := 7`), an exit that leaves a nested block and its outer one (`h := 1` in the outer, `k := 2` in the inner, both asserted), and 1000 iterations of a parallel `for`, each an exit out of an atomic block that increments one counter (`count`, asserted 1000).

The passing runs, on the final code (`eb2f652487`; the later commits change no code):

What a failed commit does, measured: the compiled test run five times at four threads with `FORTRESS_THREAD_STATISTICS=y` (`FORTRESS_THREAD_STATISTICS=y FORTRESS_THREADS=4 bin/fortress run ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`, from `ProjectFortress/`):

So the contended exits abort and run again 93 to 291 times a run, and every one of the 1000 writes is kept once. The tally counts retries only at `recordEndTransaction`, which the exit's commit now calls. In this program the body reads `count` and writes it, then exits, so an abort comes at the read's validation or at the exit's commit (`Transaction.handOver`, whose global lock fails when another block committed after the snapshot, and whose validation then finds the read stale).

## Row 1041, run once after the fix

Its behaviour stays on both paths. `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh row1041 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled.test`, on `eb2f652487`:

    . run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled (760ms) REACHED
    com.sun.fortress.runtimeSystem.LabelExit: exit from a label block that has completed
    OK (2 tests)

One consequence reaches the row's question: such an exit, run inside an atomic block, now commits that block's writes too, since neither path can tell an exit to an enclosing label from one to a label block that has completed. The program, under walk (old code through `old-fortress.sh`, new code through the worktree's `bin/fortress`, each at `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`):

    var kept: () -> () = fn (): () => ()
    var w: ZZ32 = 0
    make(): () = label gone
        kept := fn (): () => exit gone
      end gone
    run(): () = do
      make()
      try
        atomic do
          w := 5
          kept()
        end
      catch e
        LabelException => println("caught LabelException")
      end
      println("w = " w)
    end

    == ExitAfterLabelThroughAtomicProbe, old code (base), walk, one thread
    caught LabelException
    w = 0
    == ExitAfterLabelThroughAtomicProbe, new code, walk, one thread
    caught LabelException

Compiled, by reading: `leaveTransaction` commits for every `LabelExit`, and the exit then ends the program, as row 1041 says. This goes to the curator with item 562 (forCurator).

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The feature table's row for `atomic` names `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java` for the compiled transactions and `Evaluator.forAtomicExpr` with `evaluator/transactions/` for walk (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:176`); the map's B.11 says the compiled transactions live in `BaseTask`'s static methods that generated code calls, and that walk's tasks and transactions are a second, independent implementation (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:421-439`). The section names the same two places.

Precedent: no earlier change repaired an exit out of a transaction. The nearest are the two commits at a normal end, which the fix calls in the same way, and climb batch 30's `leaveTransaction` (`594da41299`), whose branch for an exception other than an abort the new branch sits beside. Sites that end a transaction: in `BaseTask.java` two, `endTransaction` (normal end) and `leaveTransaction` (abrupt end), now both committing for an exit; in walk's `FortressTaskRunner.java` one, `doItOnce`, which both of walk's callers run (`Evaluator.java:189`, `:216`). No other code of either path begins or ends a transaction: `grep -rn 'startTransaction\|endTransaction\|leaveTransaction\|doItOnce\|doIt(\|beginTransaction\|commitTransaction\|giveUpTransaction' ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress --include=*.java` prints, beside those, only the code generator's three calls (`CodeGen.java:2057`, `:2077`, `:2092`), walk's `BaseTask` methods that `doItOnce` calls, and the unit test `compiler/runtimeValues/ArrayStoreJUTest.java:41-53`, which runs a block as compiled code does and passes `leaveTransaction` only exceptions of its own body, never an exit.

The ways the implementation offers, with the one chosen (also under Decisions):

- Compiled: (a) commit in `leaveTransaction` on a `LabelExit` (chosen); (b) a second exception-table entry for `LabelExit` in `CodeGen.forAtomicBlock`, whose handler calls `endTransaction` and rethrows: its commit's abort would leave the handler outside the block's catch-all range, so it needs a third entry, and it changes every compiled atomic block's bytecode in rung O's file; (c) commit at the `exit` itself (`CodeGen.forExit`): the exit does not know which blocks it leaves when it runs in a task or a function made elsewhere (F-373).
- Walk: (a) `catch (LabelException)` in `doItOnce` (chosen); (b) in `Evaluator.forAtomicExpr`, a `Callable` that catches the exit and returns it as a marker value, rethrown after `doIt` returns: it changes rung W's file and leaves `tryatomic` without it; (c) in `doIt`: the transaction is given up by then.

## What the specification settles

`atomic.tex:59-63`: an exit retains the block's writes; an uncaught exception discards writes to objects allocated before the block, and variables revert. The second half stays as it was on both paths (`AtomicThrowRevertsCompiled` in the atomic runs; walk, the probe below). Nested blocks (`atomic.tex:72-75`) are atomic with respect to their enclosing block, so an inner commit hands its writes to the outer transaction, which the nested case asserts. `atomic.tex:46-48`: `tryatomic` "acts exactly like" `atomic` except where it throws `TryAtomicFailure`, which settles NEW-A-1. `label.tex` (section "Label and Exit") says nothing of transactions.

## Decisions

1. The compiled commit in `BaseTask.leaveTransaction`, on a `LabelExit`. Ways not taken: a `LabelExit` entry in `CodeGen.forAtomicBlock`'s exception table (its commit's abort escapes the handler's range, so a third entry; every atomic block's bytecode changes; rung O's file); a commit at `CodeGen.forExit` (an exit made in a function or a task does not know which blocks it leaves, F-373). Evidence: `CodeGen.java:2067-2100`, where the handler already takes every throwable; fork A1.
2. Walk's commit in `FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce`, in a `catch (LabelException)`. Ways not taken: a marker value through `Evaluator.forAtomicExpr` (rung W's file, and `tryatomic` would miss it); `doIt` (the transaction is given up when `doItOnce` returns). Evidence: `FortressTaskRunner.java:122-148`; `Evaluator.java:189`, `:216`.
3. A failed commit on an exit runs the block again, as at a normal end: the abort takes the existing abort path, compiled, and `AbortedException` reaches `doIt`'s retry, walk. Ways not taken: the exit leaving with the writes dropped where the commit fails (the writes of a block that did complete abruptly by an exit would be lost); an error. Evidence: fork A1 ("a failed commit runs the block again, as at a normal end"); the retry counts above.
4. The compiled exit's commit also calls `recordEndTransaction`, as `endTransaction` does, so the retry count that sets the back-off starts again after a block that committed. Way not taken: leave it, as the exception path does. Evidence: `BaseTask.java:210-221`; it changes only the statistics and the back-off.
5. A contended case in both tests, 1000 parallel exits out of a block that increments one counter, beside the section's nested case: it shows a failed commit run again. Way not taken: the nested case alone, which never aborts. Evidence: the retry counts; `tests-writing.md` asks a longer range than 16 under walk for parallelism.
6. The nested case seen failing on the base by one-run variants with the earlier assertions deleted, since the libraries' `assert` stops at the first failure (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:308-319`, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:102-105`). Way not taken: reorder the assertions, which changes the expected failure the section quotes.
7. Walk's exit out of `tryatomic` is recorded, not repaired: an `XXX` test and NEW-A-1. Way not taken: a rethrow in `Evaluator.forTryAtomicExpr`, a file the section does not name and that rung W edits. Evidence: the probe above; `Evaluator.java:229-231`.
8. The rung's ladder subset is the 8 ladder programs that hold an `atomic` block. Way not taken: the label programs of the ladder's corpus (`objectCC_label`, `LabelTest`, `exitType`, `labelExit`), whose first errors name a label, the checker or a missing name, none what this rung touched.
9. No decision of the curator names the mechanism; the rung builds fork A1's default (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-35.md:452`).

# Climb batch 35, rung A: the record lines

## Findings

1. **An exit out of an `atomic` block to an enclosing `label` now keeps the block's writes, on both paths.** Conditions: any exit (`exit` with or without a target or a `with` clause) that leaves one or more atomic blocks, at one thread and at four; a nested block's commit hands its writes to the outer transaction, whose own commit, on the same exit, stores them. Evidence: compiled, `BaseTask.leaveTransaction` commits on a `LabelExit` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:303-309`); walk, `FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce` commits on a `LabelException` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/tasks/FortressTaskRunner.java:133-141`); tests `ProjectFortress/tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss` and `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.test` (with `ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test`), which failed on the base ('FAIL: a ZZ32: 0 =/= a ZZ32: 7; writes within a block that an exit leaves are retained'; 'FAIL:  0 =/= 7; atomic.tex, section "Atomic Expressions": ...') and pass on `eb2f652487` ('OK (1 test)'; 'PASS', 'OK (3 tests)'), and at one thread by direct runs. What it means: a program may exit out of an atomic block; the workaround of a flag set in the block and an exit after it is no longer needed. Row 1039 closes.
2. **A commit that fails on an exit runs the block again, as at a normal end.** Compiled, the commit's `TransactionAbortException` takes `leaveTransaction`'s abort path (`BaseTask.java:317-322`): the block starts again where the abort names its transaction, else the abort goes on to the ancestor's block; walk, `AbortedException` reaches `doIt`'s retry. Evidence: 1000 parallel exits out of a block that increments one counter keep all 1000 writes at four threads (the tests' contended case); `FORTRESS_THREAD_STATISTICS=y FORTRESS_THREADS=4 bin/fortress run ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled` printed 'PASS Had to retry a transaction 93 times' to '291 times' over five runs. What it means: an exit out of a contended block loses no update.
3. **An exception other than an exit still discards the block's writes, on both paths.** Evidence: the gate's atomic runs, 72 of 72 `PASS` on `eb2f652487`, `AtomicThrowRevertsCompiled` among them; under walk a program with `a := 4` then `throw FailCalled("out")` in an atomic block caught outside, beside `b := 6` then an exit: 'a = 0', 'b = 6' (old code: 'a = 0', 'b = 0').
4. **An exit that runs after its label block has completed (row 1041), run inside an atomic block, now commits that block's writes too, on both paths.** Neither path can tell an exit to an enclosing label from one to a completed label block: the compiled commit is for every `LabelExit`, walk's for every `LabelException`. Evidence: under walk, `w := 5` then `kept()`, a function made in a completed `label gone` that runs `exit gone`, inside `atomic do ... end`, the whole in `try ... catch e LabelException => ...`: 'caught LabelException', 'w = 5' (old code: 'w = 0'). Compiled, by reading (`BaseTask.java:303`): the exit then ends the program, as row 1041 says; `compiler_tests/ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled.test` still passes on `eb2f652487` ('OK (2 tests)'). What it means: it belongs to row 1041's question (review-queue item 562).
5. **Under walk an exit out of a `tryatomic` block to an enclosing label never reaches its label** (NEW-A-1). `Evaluator.forTryAtomicExpr` catches every `Exception` and throws `new RuntimeException(e)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:229-231` at 13f4fdea75), the exit among them; the run dies: 'java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.RuntimeException: ...:10:7-15: exit from nonexistent label block done', on the base and after the fix. By `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:46-48` `tryatomic` acts exactly like `atomic`, so the exit reaches the label and the writes are kept. Test: `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitOutOfTryAtomicWalk.fss` (green as an expected failure; red with `atomic` in place of `tryatomic` for one run). Compiled, the program meets row 353's wall: 'Can't compile TryAtomicExpr'. What it means: write `atomic`, not `tryatomic`, around an exit.
6. **Walk's suite is unchanged by the fix:** `ant testSystem` on `eb2f652487`, 879 tests in four shards (214, 228, 216, 221), 0 failures, the count of the last landed gate (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-34b/gate/summary.txt`).

## For FACTS

**An exit out of an `atomic` block commits the block's transaction, on both paths, and keeps its writes.** Compiled, the block's handler `BaseTask.leaveTransaction` commits on a `LabelExit` as `endTransaction` does at a normal end; walk's `FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce` commits on a `LabelException` as at a normal end. A commit that fails runs the block again, as at a normal end, and an exception other than an exit still discards the writes. A nested block's commit hands its writes to the outer one. So a program may exit out of an atomic block (atomic.tex, section "Atomic Expressions"); an exit that runs after its label block completed commits the blocks it passes too (row 1041). Tests: `tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`, `compiler_tests/ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-exit-out-of-atomic/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "The tests: failing on the base, passing after".

Change to F-373: its sentence "Four limits stand, each with its test: an exit out of an `atomic` block loses the block's writes (row 1039); a `finally` clause ..." becomes "Three limits stand, each with its test: a `finally` clause ...", the rest as it is; row 1039 is fixed (the entry above).

## For the gather

- `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/SKILL.md:126`, "An `exit` out of an `atomic` block loses the block's writes, on both paths (ledger row 1039). Set a flag in the block, and exit after the block.", is false after this rung (the skill writer's, from "Revival change" below).

## Handover

Climb batch 35 rung A (`wip/rung-exit-out-of-atomic`, `eb2f652487`, `8bd7cfcf0a`): an exit out of an atomic block commits the block's transaction on both paths (a failed commit runs the block again; an exception still discards), row 1039 closes with its two tests promoted; NEW-A-1 opens, walk's exit out of `tryatomic` lost in a `RuntimeException`, with its `XXX` test; row 1041 gains the consequence that such an exit commits the blocks it passes, for item 562.

## Revival change

The change: the team's walk runs an atomic block in `FortressTaskRunner.doItOnce`, which commits the block's transaction only after the body ends normally and gives it up uncommitted in its `finally` when anything leaves the body (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/tasks/FortressTaskRunner.java:121-138` at 13f4fdea75), so an `exit` (a `LabelException`) out of the block lost the block's writes. The compiled path's handler, `BaseTask.leaveTransaction`, did the same: it ended the transaction without a commit for anything but an abort (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:293-314` at 13f4fdea75). The tree now commits the block's transaction when an exit leaves it, on both paths, and an exit that leaves a nested block and its outer one commits both; a commit that fails runs the block again; an exception other than an exit still discards the writes. Tests: `ProjectFortress/tests/ExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss` and `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.test`. The reason: the specification, "If it completes abruptly by exiting to an enclosing \KWD{label} expression, writes within the block are retained and become visible to other threads." (`Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:60-63`), and the measured failure on the base: 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 0 =/= a ZZ32: 7; writes within a block that an exit leaves are retained' (walk), 'FAIL:  0 =/= 7; ...' (compiled). An exit that runs after its label block has completed commits the blocks it passes as well, since neither path tells it from an exit to an enclosing label. Under walk an exit out of a `tryatomic` block still dies before its label.
